finding: Unanswered UDP/DNS bursts (Generic attacks) are the largest threat by volume
evidence: udp/dns/INT segment: 57,692 flows, 99.9% malicious; 98.6% of DNS attack flows are Generic; sub-ms flows are 91.3% attacks
recommended_action: Enable DNS response-rate limiting, block unsolicited inbound DNS from untrusted sources, alert on bursts of INT-state (no-reply) UDP flows to the same host/service

finding: Exploit traffic concentrates on classic application services
evidence: Exploits dominate attack flows on http (65% of 17,650), smtp (89% of 4,695), ftp (70% of 3,004), ftp-data (99% of 1,890)
recommended_action: Prioritise patching of web, mail and FTP servers; put HTTP behind a WAF/IPS with exploit signatures; disable plaintext POP3/FTP where possible

finding: Uncommon IP protocols are almost always malicious
evidence: 34,814 flows use protocols outside ['arp', 'ospf', 'tcp', 'udp']; 99.8% are attacks. Rare-protocol rule fires on 17.9% of attacks vs 0.08% of normal flows
recommended_action: Default-deny non-essential IP protocols at the perimeter and on internal segments; alert on any allowed exception

finding: Supervised detector catches almost every attack but raises many false alarms on new traffic
evidence: LightGBM: recall 97.3%, PR-AUC 0.989, but FPR 17.9% (6,627 false alarms on 37,000 normal test flows) - train/test distribution shift
recommended_action: Triage by risk bucket rather than raw model alerts: Critical-bucket precision is 99.4% on 36,870 flows. Re-tune the threshold on recent local traffic and retrain regularly

finding: The model leans heavily on TTL, a lab-specific artefact
evidence: sttl mean abs SHAP 3.69 vs ct_state_ttl 0.98; sttl/dttl 254/0 is 92.4% attacks
recommended_action: Before production use, validate on your own network captures and test a model without TTL features; treat UNSW-NB15 accuracy as an upper bound

finding: Unsupervised anomaly detection misses stealthy and payload-based attacks
evidence: Isolation Forest flags 96.7% of Generic and 77.4% of DoS flows, but only 11.9% of Reconnaissance, 3.7% of Shellcode and 20.5% of Worms
recommended_action: Keep anomaly scoring as one layer (novelty detection) alongside signatures/IDS rules and the supervised model - never as the only control

finding: Attack-type labels for DoS / Analysis / Backdoor are unreliable
evidence: Multiclass F1: DoS 0.26, Analysis 0.02, Backdoor 0.07 (vs Generic 0.98) - their flow features overlap heavily
recommended_action: Use the binary attack score for alerting and treat predicted category as a hint; enrich these alerts with payload/host context before escalation

finding: Visibility gap: no IPs, ports or timestamps in this dataset version
evidence: IP-level risk, true port-scan counts (distinct dsport per srcip) and peak attack hours could not be computed; segment-level substitutes were used
recommended_action: Ingest the full UNSW-NB15 release or production NetFlow/Zeek logs with IPs and timestamps to enable per-host risk, scan detection and time-based alerting
